Title: Obligatory Spider-Man Post
Author: Kayode D. '27
Article Content:
[this blog is so so late, but it’s about the goat and i need to post it, so here it is!!:]

Last night, I went with some friends to watch Spider-Man Brand New Day at the movie theater. I LOVED IT. I think it’s the best on yet, and my favorite movie of the year hands down. I’ve been thinking about going back to watch it again tonight…

I was telling my mom about it, and she said I should make a blog pointing out the MIT references the movie had, and there were a good few!! Light spoilers ahead and heavy spoilers at the end of this blog.

MIT References [Light Spoilers]

In Spider-Man No Way Home, Ned and MJ get accepted to MIT in the class of 2028. Spider-Man does not get to go because of space-time hijinx, and spends the next 4 years watching them enjoy MIT through Ned’s social media. We don’t get to see much of MIT[1] , as all we get is a montage of the years passing. There is one notable exception.

Towards the end of their time at MIT, Ned says the line:

“Final Semester at MIT! Oh, my gosh we’re graduating in a month. We’ve made so many memories. Where do I begin? Night swimming in the Charles River with Jim and Wiley. The infamous food fight at the banana lounge. Pulling all-nighters at Stud 5 with MJ and Nate Dawg. It seems like yesterday I was sitting on a roof with MJ…”

So much to unpack here. Let’s break it down:

- Night Swimming in the Charles River: Very much not recommended. The Charles river is not clean enough to swim in, especially not at night. I know someone who was doing a research study on the bacteria growing in the river…all I’m saying is that this one isn’t a flex.
- Infamous Food Fight at the Banana Lounge: The Banana Lounge is a space on campus where large crates of bananas are regularly delivered. There is definitely the ammo for this, but the space is pretty tight to constitute a full on food fight. It would be very notable, though.
- Pulling all nighters at Stud 5: This one had us losing our minds. This is elite ball knowledge. The other two you could make up with some google searches but to know about stud 5?? Stud 5 is the fifth floor of the Student Center, a big study space where students often pull all nighters, especially during the end of the semesters.[2] but for them to mention this in the movie?? ELITE Ball knowledge. I wonder who they talked to to get that line. Has to have been a student or someone. Hmmmm…

Other than that, there isn’t much else mentioned about MIT in the movie. There is one other thing I took note on: At one part, MJ tells Peter that before she switched to studying Aero-astro, she wanted to study Biochemical Engineering. She then looks at his device and solves an issue. While walking home after the movie, I realized that there are very few [if any at all] classes that overlap in these two majors. To switch from course 10B to 16 would be a full academic career pivot, and one she would have to take before her sophomore year in order to take Unified, a series of Aero-Astro classes that most course 16’s take their sophomore year. So this means she only got at most a year of focused Biochemical engineering courses, which I’d wager isn’t enough to make the jumps and problem solving required to repair Peter’s tech. Unless she ASE’d out of all of her GIRs and did a full year of advanced biochemistry, and then FULL PIVOTED out of that into Aero-Astro…which is possible…or she did UROPs and independent research in that area while studying course 16…or if this is a superhero movie that I am overanalyzing in the nerdiest way possible.

Also, no one was wearing their brass rats. Which is fair, people don’t wear them all the time, but still. Ok, MIT nerd nitpicking over.

ABSOLUTE CINEMA

This movie was SO PEAK. From Beginning to END!!!

I think that this was the best superhero movie that I have seen…possibly ever. I felt like a kid again!! Watching Spidey beat the bad guys! And I like how they handled the power-creep this time around. We just finished arcs where Spider-Man was battling Thanos. It’s hard to make Batroc the Leaper feel like a gratifying next villain after the last one almost destroyed the planet. But they did it! A street-level Spider-man. Who woulda thunk? And the whole arc with MJ??? So many layers to it, such a good movie.

Also, I LOVE THE MOVIES!! What?? I forgot how much fun the movies are. We went to the AMC in Boston Commons, near downtown. It was BUSTLING with people–mainly teens and college students– and it was a really fun time. In high school I worked at a pizza place, but if I ever left that job I wanted to work at the movie theater. I need to go back ASAP.

Lowkey, I started this blog in July and didn’t finish it. Now I did, but I forget most of what I thought about this movie other than it’s good. I’d watch it again. Maybe I will and then I can make more comments on why it’s good. Happy Birthday, Maynard!

Title: bringing my digicam to class for a “week”
Author: Veronica P. '27
Article Content:
Hi blog,

I am an avid user of what kids these days are calling a digi— those digital cameras from the 2000’s that fit in your pocket, can document the date in the bottom right corner, and have a somewhat-unreliable flash system. [1] I think a big part of the appeal is the nostalgia— the photos look like the ones you covet of your parents before you came around, when they were young and fun and carefree. As college students, now is our prescribed time to be young, fun and carefree. What better way to document it than with a digi?!

Now, despite being my inspiration, my parents absolutely cannot get behind this. Isn’t the whole point of a phone that you have all of these devices in one? [2] Why do you keep spending so much money on old things? [3] And, admittedly, I have blown through about 3 E-bay cameras in my time, but I have absolutely no regrets! My phone is an exhausting, anxiety-inducing time-suck at least half of the time. The more I can do to reduce my dependence on that rectangular prism, the better. As for the ‘old’ stuff: it’s taking up space in this world anyways, why not give it a new life? [4]

However, I’ve come upon a recent dilemma with my digi usage. This whole young, fun, and carefree expectation I’ve put around it has made it such that my camera only really gets its mileage at 10 PM on a Friday. Or when I’m on vacation. These photos are great, but as a senior who is hyper-aware of her senior-ness I find that I want to capture every aspect of my life at MIT, not just the weekends.

So, I set out to bring my digi-cam everywhere for a whole week of school. Let’s see how it went.

monday

a morning view of my suite! my roommate and i both ate breakfast on our desks. at 11:30, i hop onto a zoom to meet with the teaching team for 2.006, the course i TA, and eat leftover free thai food for lunch

i have 2.009 (Product Engineering Processes) lecture and lab from 1-5pm, and this week we chose officer roles. i'm a system integrator, whose job is to coordinate amongst all of our subteams/task forces, plan lab agendas, keep our timeline on track, and help each of our subassemblies combine into a larger product. i forget to bring my digi out until the evening, when i'm prepping to hold office hours. two of my friends from floor are regular attendees!

back in the suite, Emily P. '28 endeavors to make a loaf of banana bread for the floor. everyone is very happy!!!

monday, again?

After this first semi-successful day, I completely forgot to bring my camera around for the rest of the week. So, I present to you: more Monday. I wore the same outfit, totally for continuity and not by accident at all…

good morning, ft. my roommate's unique seating choices

my walk to the (newly opened) met warehouse

a quick look inside as i get a latte from the cafe on the first floor. i take my teaching team meeting at some tables by the entrance and do some research on fellowships.

a shot of 2.009 lecture before it's time to head into pappalardo lab! my team selected our final product concept today, which was a very long discussion. i'll leave more details about this product for a later blog!

i come home to a few floor members doing work together! i hang out, eat dinner, and chat before i head out to office hours.

tuesday…

Not for lack of remembering, I chose not to document my Tuesday this week. After office hours on Monday, I started to do work grad school applications and, realizing just how real and imminent they were, began to feel incredibly overwhelmed and out of my depth. It was a rough night, and I felt even worse the next morning. In the afternoon, I had my weekly meeting with the grad student who supervises my UROP. I expressed a few of these feelings, and she was sweet enough to dedicate the hour to giving me guidance and support I needed to get back on track. Perhaps a blog for another time! I called my dad to update him on my talk, spent some time with my friend in Hayden, and then headed to a Mech-E grad school info session, motivation renewed.

wednesday

In the morning, I showed up to the booths in Lobby 10 to help Camp Kesem (also a blog for another time) promote their application cycle! I got free coffee and was able to catch up with a few counselors. I then went to Barker to send out a few grad-application emails I had been putting off, and then spent some time in Pappalardo preparing for the 2.009 build challenge on Friday (many, many photos to come). In the evening, I had System Integrator training for 2.009. Having lost my momentum, I didn’t document much.

I did manage to get one photo, though…

the bloggers!!! wrapping up our biweekly blog meeting. ft. many masks because freshman flu is real…

thursday

Okay, wow, I’m bad at this. I had a wave demo lab for 2.016 (Hydrodynamics) and drawing for designers class.

friday

BUILD CHALLENGE DAY!!! All of the 2.009 teams gather onto Killian Court to compete on a challenge course using cardboard devices. These devices had to move our teams payload (puzzle pieces) 16′ at a time as quickly as possible, without leaving the loading/unloading zones.

We were given the following materials: cardboard, paper tape, wooden dowels, cotton robe, and two-five gallon buckets of water.

Our two devices had the following unique requirements:

Device 1: Can only touch the group in loading/unloading zones and a 3′ x 3′ box on the ground in the middle. This ended up being our school bus!

device 1: one long rope remains in tension to hang the device above the ground, while two ropes on either side can be pulled to move the device towards the loading/unloading zones!

Device 2: Can only have one actuated rotational degree of freedom. This was our Lightning McQueen!.

our device 2, lightning mcqueen! we used ropes to spin the axle of the front and back wheels.

However, the prize isn’t actually for moving the most puzzle pieces the fastest, it’s for team spirit! So, here’s some photos of Red Team on the competition course, featuring my teammate’s digi as well!

red team on the course!!!! we ended up finishing first, and blue team won the prize for team spirit!

And there we have it! Sort of a week in my life, through my digi lens. Everyone knows that social media only captures the highs, but I really underestimated how difficult it would be for me to photograph the lows and the room-temperatures of the week. I’d love to attempt this again, with more than 3 days to show for myself. For now, however, I’m glad to have these snapshots to look back on, and remember when I was young, selectively fun, and definitely not carefree.
